title: The impact of peritraumatic perception on the formation of intrusive memories
summary:
The aim of the study is to test a leading theory on the formation and
 treatment of trauma-associated intrusive memories.
For this purpose, healthy volunteers are subjected to a potentially stressful scenario presented in virtual reality. Depending on the experimental group,
the scene is presented from different perspectives, in order to  systematically examine the influences of different perception modes on the occurrence
of intrusive memories. In parallel, heart rate and electrodermal activity are recorded. After the experiment, the number and intensities of subsequent intrusive memories are recorded over a period of one week using a smartphone app.
The assumption is that at group level the number (and possibly
the intensity ) of intrusive memories differ in relation to respective modes of perception. In addition, it is expected
that skin conductivity and heart rate will also differ between the modalities of perception during stimulus presentation.

interventions.name:
A number of 150 healthy volunteers between the ages of 18 and 65 will be included in the study.
